identity.retryPolicy: Transport failures (timeout (180s), network error, HTTP 408/409/429/5xx, unreadable API response with 5xx, incomplete or missing output) are retried up to 4 attempts per turn with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After and provider reset headers. Live calls use a 5-second minimum pace, increasing automatically to stay under 80% of a reported token/minute limit, and live episodes cool down by 30 seconds; every attempt and sanitized rate-limit header is recorded. Exhausted HTTP 429 retries interrupt the batch as infrastructure rather than counting as model failure. Invalid model output (unparseable JSON, schema violation, refusal) is not retried or repaired: it is recorded as an invalid response and terminates the episode as unsolved. A valid direction that is visibly blocked is not retried or repaired: it is executed as a blocked move, counts as a wall hit, consumes the turn, and the episode continues.

aiTransport.policy: Provider requests use the shared Vercel AI SDK transport with structured output. SDK retries are disabled; Echo Maze owns every retry, pacing delay, and attempt record.

identity.coordinateSystem: Walker-relative coordinates start at (0,0). A successful move right changes x by +1, left by -1, up by +1, down by -1. A blocked move changes nothing. The Walker never receives absolute maze rows/columns.
identity.hiddenStatePolicy: The prompt receives only the narrow observation DTO (open/blocked directions, corridor sightlines, per-visible-cell open directions and isExit flag, last action/result) plus the current run's conversation. No full maze, no exit coordinates, no seed, no optimal route, no unseen cells, and no spectator state may enter the prompt.

payload.notes: Start (0,0). Open up/right/left; down blocked. Exploring left corridor first and tracking coordinates from successful moves.
At (-1,0), horizontal corridor. Left sight reaches three cells to a terminal-looking cell; right has a branch upward one cell away. Continue left to map the corridor endpoint before backtracking.
At (-2,0), continuing left along the corridor toward its terminal cell. No branches observed on this segment; map the endpoint before backtracking.
At (-3,0). Continue left to the corridor endpoint; the visible cell to the left appears terminal with only a right exit. Then backtrack and investigate branches to the right.
At (-4,0), the left corridor endpoint has been reached. Backtrack right toward the nearest unexplored upward branch, likely around x=-1.
At (-3,0), backtracking right from the left endpoint. The next unexplored upward branch is approximately two moves right, near x=-1; continue toward it.
At (-2,0), backtracking right toward the upward branch visible two cells ahead near (-1,0). Continue right once more before exploring upward.
At (-1,0). The upward branch is one cell to the right, at the starting cell (0,0). Move right to reach it, then explore upward.
At (0,0), returned from the left corridor. The upward branch is open and unexplored; proceed upward to map it.
At (0,1) after moving up. The upward route is blocked, while right leads to an unexplored branch cell with an upward opening; explore right before backtracking.
At (1,1), the right branch ends and down returns to the previously visited cell. Move up into the unexplored branch; track position as (1,2) after success.
At (1,2), up and right are blocked. The unexplored route continues left; the sightline shows two cells, with the farther one branching down. Move left to investigate.
At (0,2), moved left from (1,2). Continue left along the unexplored upper corridor toward the visible branching cell; track any exit or new route.
At (-1,2) after moving left from (0,2). Right returns along the explored upper corridor; down is the only unexplored branch. Explore downward.
At (-1,1) after moving down from the upper corridor. Up returns to the explored route; left is the remaining unexplored direction. Move left and update position to (-2,1).
At (-2,1), moved left into the remaining branch. Right returns to the explored route; up leads to an unexplored cell, so continue upward and map that branch.
At (-2,2), upward move succeeded. Down returns to the explored branch; left is the remaining unexplored direction. Continue left to map this route.
At (-4,2), the leftward branch ends. Right returns to the explored cell; down is the only unexplored direction. Explore downward.
At (-4,1) after moving down from the upper branch. Up returns to the explored cell; left is unexplored and open. Continue left to map the remaining route.
At (-5,1) after moving left. Left is blocked; right returns to the explored branch. Move up into the remaining unexplored route and inspect for the exit.
At (-5,3), the vertical route continues upward into an unexplored cell; down returns to the mapped branch. Continue upward and inspect the next junction for the exit.
At (-5,4), upward route is blocked. Right leads to an unexplored junction, while down returns to the mapped branch. Explore right first.
At (-4,4) after moving right from the upper endpoint. Left returns to the prior cell; up is the remaining unexplored direction. Continue upward and inspect for the exit.
At (-4,5); up and right are blocked. Down returns to the previously mapped cell, while left leads to the remaining unexplored branch. Move left to continue exploration.
At (-5,5) after moving left. Down and left are blocked; right returns to the mapped branch, while up leads to an unexplored cell with a right/down junction. Continue upward to explore.
At (-5,6) after moving up. Up and left are blocked; right leads to an unexplored branch, while down returns to the mapped route. Explore right.
At (-4,6) after moving right. Right and down are blocked; left returns to the prior branch, while up leads to the unexplored route. Continue upward to search for the exit.
At the new upper cell after the last upward move. Up and right are blocked; down returns to the prior branch, while left is unexplored. Continue left to search for the exit.
At the new cell after moving left. Up and right are open; the upward sightline extends two cells and remains unexplored, so continue upward to map this branch.
At (-5,8) after moving up. The upward cell is a dead end, while down returns to the prior junction. Explore the dead-end first, then backtrack to investigate the downward branch.
Backtracked from the dead end at (-5,8). At (-5,7), the upward route is exhausted; investigate the remaining right branch next.
At (-5,7) after backtracking from the dead end. Only down is open, leading to the previously noted junction at (-5,6), where the unexplored right branch should be investigated next.
At (-5,6), back at the junction after exhausting the upward dead end. The right branch remains unexplored; move right to investigate it.
At (-4,6) after moving right. Both open directions appear to lead back through explored cells; backtrack downward to continue systematic exploration toward any missed branch.

At the current cell after moving down from the upper branch. Open routes are up and left; the downward route has returned to a previously explored-looking structure. Continue upward to investigate the remaining branch systematically.
At the upper branch cell after moving up. Up and right are blocked; down returns to the mapped route, while left leads to the remaining branch. Continue left to explore it.
At the junction matching the earlier (-5,6) cell after moving left. The upper branch is exhausted; right returns to the connected branch. Move right, then seek a route away from the loop.
At (-4,6), both exits are known loop connections. Move down to continue back through the explored structure and search for any missed branch or exit.
At the current junction after moving down. Up returns through the explored upper loop; left is the remaining alternative route. Move left to continue systematic exploration.

At (-5,4), the left move returned to the known upper endpoint. Up and left are blocked; right is the explored loop, while down leads back toward the lower structure and any remaining unexplored branches. Continue down.
At the current cell after moving down. Up appears to lead back through the explored upper structure; right is the remaining unexplored branch. Explore right and update the map from its result.
At (-4,3) after the successful right move. Both open directions lead into connected explored-looking corridors; choose left to inspect the adjacent branch and continue searching for an exit.
At the branch cell reached after moving up from (-5,3). The surrounding upper loop has been explored, so continue through the known rightward connection and reassess for any missed route.
The last upward move succeeded into a junction with right and down open. Continue right to inspect the adjacent branch and avoid repeating the upper loop.

At the junction after moving right. Both available directions appear connected to previously explored loop cells; take the left branch to continue traversal and look for an overlooked exit or alternate connection.
At the current junction with right and down open. The upper loop appears explored; take the downward route to return toward the lower structure and search for an unvisited branch or exit.
At the junction after moving down. Up returns through the upper loop; right enters the adjacent connected branch. Continue right to traverse the remaining structure and search for the exit.
At (-4,3) after the successful right move. Both down and left are open and connect to the explored loop; take down to continue tracing the lower structure and look for an unvisited branch or exit.

At the current junction after moving down. Both up and left are open; the surrounding lower loop has been traversed repeatedly, so take the upward route to inspect the adjacent branch for an overlooked exit.

At the cell reached after moving up from the lower junction. Up and right are blocked; down returns to the junction, while left is the remaining unexplored-looking branch. Continue left to escape the repeated loop.
At (-5,3) after moving left. Up and right are open; the adjacent structure has been revisited, but take the upward route to continue systematic exploration and avoid the immediate loop.
At (-5,4) after the successful upward move. Both available routes are part of the explored loop; take down to return toward the lower junction and search for any missed branch.
At (-5,3) after moving down. The upward route returns through the loop, so take the open right branch and reassess the connected structure for an overlooked exit.
At (-4,3), the loop offers down and left. Down enters the lower junction and is the best remaining direction to trace for an unseen exit; avoid repeating the upper loop.
At the current junction, up returns into the repeatedly traversed loop. Move left along the adjacent branch toward the lower-left structure, which remains the best route for finding an unseen exit.

At the current junction after moving left. Right appears to lead into a short dead-end branch, while down extends through two cells and is the best remaining route toward unexplored structure. Continue down.

Moved down from the junction into the vertical corridor. Down remains open and the sightline shows one intermediate cell before a branching cell, so continue downward to investigate the remaining route.
At (-5,-2) after moving down. Down and left are blocked; right is the remaining unexplored branch, while up returns through the known corridor. Explore right.
At (-4,-2) after moving right. Right and down are blocked; up leads back through the known corridor, while left enters the remaining unexplored branch. Move left to investigate it.
At (-5,-2) after returning left from (-4,-2). Up is known; left is the remaining unexplored branch. Continue left to investigate it.

Left was blocked, confirming the current cell. Right returns to a previously visited side cell; move up through the known corridor toward the junction at (-5,0), where the right branch remains insufficiently explored.
At (-5,-1), up returns to the junction at (-5,0); down leads back through the explored lower corridor. Move up, then investigate the junction’s rightward route more carefully.
At (-5,0), move right into the adjacent branch cell. This route has not been directly traversed from this junction; inspect its upward opening for a possible exit or unexplored continuation.
At (-4,0) after moving right from the junction. The current cell has an unexplored-looking upward route; move up to inspect it before backtracking.
At (-4,1), both open routes connect to previously seen structure. Take left to continue systematic traversal toward any missed branch or exit; update position to (-5,1) if successful.
At (-5,1), both up and right are open. Right returns through the repeatedly traversed loop, so continue upward to inspect the remaining connected route for an unseen exit.
At (-5,2) after moving up. Down returns to the explored lower corridor; right leads to the adjacent branch cell and is the best remaining route to inspect for an unseen exit.
At (-4,2); right and down are blocked, while up and left connect to previously traversed corridors. Continue upward through the loop toward the central junction, then reassess for any missed branch.

At the current cell after moving up. Both down and left are open and previously traversed, but left continues toward the central junction and may expose a missed connection; proceed left while maintaining the coordinate estimate.

At (-5,3) after moving left. Up and right are open but both connect to previously traversed structure. Take the upward route to continue systematic exploration and check the next junction for any missed exit.
At (-5,4) after moving up from (-5,3). Up leads to a known dead end; down returns toward the junction and remaining lower structure. Backtrack down to continue systematic exploration.
At (-5,3). The upward branch leads to a confirmed dead end; take right into the adjacent junction, then continue through its downward route to search the remaining lower structure.

At the cell reached after moving down from the recurring junction. The visible lower cell branches up/left; continue down to trace the lower structure and search for an exit rather than repeating the upper loop.
At (-4,1) after moving down. Up returns to the recurring junction; left is the only alternate route and should be followed to continue tracing the lower structure for an unseen exit.
At approximately (-5,1) after the last left move. Right returns to the repeatedly traversed loop; take the open downward route toward the lower structure, continuing the search for an unseen exit.

At the lower endpoint after moving down. Right leads to the previously inspected side cell, while up returns through the vertical corridor toward the junction. Backtrack up and reassess the remaining route.

The current observation matches the earlier upper junction pattern. Move right into the adjacent branch and inspect its connected route, avoiding another immediate backtrack along the vertical corridor.
At (-4,-1) after moving right. Right and down are blocked; left returns to the lower corridor, while up is the remaining route toward the central structure. Continue upward to inspect it.

At the junction reached after moving up. Up and right are blocked; both down and left connect to known corridors. Move left to continue systematic exploration toward the central structure and avoid the recently traversed lower branch.
At (-6,0) after moving left from the junction. Up and right are open; right likely returns to the known corridor, so explore upward as the remaining unvisited route.
At (-6,1) after moving up. The cell above is a dead end with only a down connection, so backtrack down to (-6,0) and continue exploring the remaining rightward route.

At (-6,0) after backtracking from the dead-end above. The upward branch is exhausted; move right into the known junction and then continue along its lower/right alternatives to search for any missed exit.

At the junction matching the previously visited (-5,0) cell. Left returns to the exhausted dead-end branch; move down through the lower corridor to continue systematic exploration and avoid repeating the upper loop.
At the current junction with up and left open. The upward branch appears previously traversed; move left to continue through the remaining connected structure and search for an exit.
At the current cell after moving left. Up and left are blocked; right returns toward the known corridor, while down is the remaining unexplored direction. Continue down to search for the exit.
At (-7,-3) after moving down. Up returns to the previously visited junction; right is the remaining unexplored branch. Explore right and track the new corridor.

At the newly reached branch cell after moving right. Up and right are blocked; left returns to the prior corridor, while down is the remaining unexplored direction. Continue down and update the position.
At the current cell after moving down. Up returns to the prior branch; right and down are blocked. Take the open left route to continue exploring the remaining corridor.
Moved left into the current branch cell, estimated at (-7,-4). Right returns to the prior corridor; down is the remaining unexplored direction. Continue downward to map this branch.
At the current vertical corridor after moving down. Both up and down are open; the downward sightline reaches a branching cell, so continue down to explore the remaining route.
Down move succeeded into a junction. The downward route is now behind me; right leads to a nearby branch cell with an upward opening and appears least explored. Move right to inspect it.
At the branch cell reached by moving right from the lower junction. Left returns to the known corridor; up is the remaining unexplored route. Continue upward and inspect for a new branch or exit.
At the newly reached cell after moving up. Right and down are open; the right cell appears to continue into an unexplored branch, while down returns toward the prior lower corridor. Explore right.
At the new branch cell after moving right. Up and right are blocked; left returns to the prior cell, while down leads into the remaining unexplored route. Continue downward to inspect it.
At (-5,-6) after moving down. Both up and right are open; up returns to the recently traversed branch, while right leads to a new-looking cell with an upward opening. Explore right.
At (-4,-6) after moving right. Right and down are blocked; left returns to the prior branch, while up is the remaining unexplored route. Continue upward to inspect for the exit.
At (-4,-5) after moving up. Up and left are blocked; right extends through two cells, while down leads back toward the recently traversed lower branch. Explore right for a possible exit or new route.
At (-3,-5) after moving right. Continue right along the visible horizontal corridor toward the farther branching cell; this route remains unexplored and may reveal the exit.
At (-2,-5), continuing right along the unexplored horizontal corridor. The next cell branches down and left, so move right to inspect that junction for a route toward the exit.
At (-2,-5); the attempted right move was blocked. Left returns along the mapped corridor, while down is the remaining unexplored branch shown by the sightline. Move down to investigate it.
At (-2,-6) after moving down from the horizontal corridor. Up returns to the known route; left leads to the next unexplored cell and may reveal a continuation or exit. Explore left.
At (-3,-6) after moving left. Up and left are blocked; right returns to the known horizontal corridor, while down is the remaining unexplored branch. Continue downward to search for the exit.

At (-3,-7) after moving down. Down is blocked; all other directions are open. The left corridor extends four cells and appears least explored, so continue left to map its endpoint and search for the exit.

At (-4,-7) after moving left. The left corridor extends three cells to a terminal-looking endpoint with only a right exit; continue left to inspect its endpoint, then backtrack to investigate the upward branch to the right.

At (-5,-7), continuing left toward the corridor endpoint. The left sightline shows two more cells, with the terminal cell appearing to have only a right exit. Inspect the endpoint before backtracking to the upward branch on the right.
At (-5,-7), continue left to inspect the corridor endpoint. After mapping the terminal cell, backtrack right toward the upward branch and unexplored continuation.
At the left corridor endpoint; only right is open. Backtrack right along the corridor toward the unexplored upward branch and continue systematic exploration.
At (-5,-7), backtracking right from the left endpoint. The corridor shows an upward branch three cells ahead, so continue right toward that unexplored branch.
At (-5,-7), moving right along the corridor toward the upward branch visible three cells ahead. Continue mapping this lower-left route and inspect the branch when reached.
At (-3,-7), continuing right toward the visible upward branch three cells ahead. This lower-left corridor remains unexplored; advance right and inspect the branch when reached.
At (-3,-7), move right toward the nearby junction whose first cell has an upward opening. Explore that branch next, while continuing to track the lower-left corridor systematically.
At approximately (-2,-7); right is open toward a nearby horizontal junction whose farther cell has an upward opening. Continue right to reach and inspect that branch.
Moved right from the lower-left corridor to the junction at (0,-7). The adjacent right cell has an upward opening, so continue right to reach that branch and then explore upward.
At (0,-7) after the blocked right attempt. The right branch is inaccessible from here; move up into the adjacent unexplored cell, whose visible openings include a possible rightward continuation.
At (0,-6), up and left are blocked. Move right into the unexplored adjacent branch; its visible cell has an upward opening, so inspect that route next.
At (1,-6) after moving right. The current corridor runs left-right; the cell to the right has up, down, and left openings, making it the next unexplored junction. Move right to inspect it.

At (2,-6) after moving right into the junction. Right is blocked; left returns to the known corridor, while up and down are unexplored from this cell. Explore upward first for a possible exit or continuation.

At (2,-5) after moving up from the junction. Up continues one cell to a branch with a left opening, while down returns to the known junction. Continue upward to inspect the remaining route for the exit.
At (2,-5). Continue upward into the visible branch cell; it has a left opening that may lead to an unexplored route or the exit. Down returns to the known junction.
Up is blocked at the current junction. Move left into the adjacent unexplored cell, then follow any new branch revealed there; down is the known return route.
